question: New job: part SM-106 (Sensor mount plate, new job), material 6061-T6 aluminum, qty 30, 6 features, deepest pocket 12 mm, 6 holes, plate 126 cm2. Using ONLY Keewano history: (1) which toolpath strategies should the CAM search try first for this part (rank by simulated cycle time on the most similar past parts, especially by pocket depth; drop strategies that failed verification or never win), (2) which supplier to buy a missing aluminum blank from (delivered price vs lead days from past quotes), (3) which step of the order is the bottleneck (StepSeconds), (4) before vs after: agent programming time vs the manual estimate, best vs manual-baseline machine time. Then call final_decision.

answer.supplier_reason: Cheapest delivered price on every past quote: SM-101 $266.75 vs Pacific Metals $334.70, FTC-10 $47.60 vs $86.70. Lead time is 2 days vs 0 for Pacific on SM-101, so use Pacific only if the blank is needed the same day.
answer.before_after: Programming: 14400 s (4 h manual estimate) vs 3 s agent JobProgrammedSeconds on SM-106. Machine: manual-baseline 1855 s (30:55) vs best adaptive-so45-ap2D 218 s (3:38), 88% saved per part, about 13.6 h saved over 30 parts.
answer.summary: SM-106 has been run twice before at 12 mm pocket depth. Both times adaptive-so45-ap2D won and passed verification at 218 s, against 1855 s for the manual-style program, so the CAM search should try it first, then adaptive-so35-ap2D (220 s) and conventional-so60-ap1D (234 s). Buy the blank from Bay Alloy & Steel (cheapest on every past quote, 2-day lead). The slowest step is the supplier phone calls (885 s total), not CAM.
